newsitem.title: UK: London U.S. stocks firm, build on Friday's rally.
newsitem.headline: London U.S. stocks firm, build on Friday's rally.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London continued Friday's Wall Street rebound after in-line payroll data eased the market's worst fears about the strength of the U.S economy, traders said. Business remained modest, however, with investors still wary about inflation and eyeing the Federal reserve Open market Committee meeting on September 24.
Little significant economic data is due today and U.S. stocks are expected to build upon Friday's advance at the open.
Sentiment in London was also helped by remarks by a Federal Reserve official on Sunday.
Fed governor Lawrence Meyer said that one single employment report would not determine the outcome of a Fed monetary policy meeting.
While many are now expecting a hike in U.S. rates after the meeting, Friday's data made a 25 basis point rise more likely than the 50 some were beginning to fear, traders said.
With the election approaching, others still suspect the Fed may hold off from raising rates in the near term.
Among individual movers, Woolworths added $1/2 to $21-1/4, while auto stocks lost ground on negative press comment on General Motors, which slipped $3/8 to $47-3/8, traders said.

"The index futures are looking firm and the bonds are OK as well. The market looks like it'll continue Friday's performance. Inflation, growth and interest rates are still the focus at the moment so it's not going to shoot away," said a trader.
On Friday, the Dow ended nearly 53 points higher at 5659.86.
